title: Register for and pay payroll tax
what: Register with the state revenue office and pay payroll tax once wages paid in Australia pass the state's threshold.

sources.title: Payroll Tax Act 2007 (NSW)
sources.publisher: NSW Legislation (via the Open Australian Legal Corpus)
sources.quote: An employer who is not already registered must apply for registration as an employer under this Act if— (a) during a month in a financial year the employer pays or is liable to pay, anywhere, wages of more than the weekly threshold amount per week that are wholly or partly taxable wages,

triggers.unit: AUD of taxable wages a financial year (annual threshold)
triggers.note: Registration is triggered month by month, when wages pass the monthly or weekly equivalent; groups share one threshold.

confidence_note: Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the version shown (DECISIONS E-118); later changes not checked.

assessment.summary: A tax on wages above a tax-free threshold. The threshold makes it a tax on growing past a certain size, and exemptions narrow the base; a broad, flat payroll tax would distort less.

marks.reason: The threshold is a tax on growing past it, which can hold firms below it.
Thresholds and exemptions make the tax fall unevenly across employers, distorting hiring and firm size.

assessment.confidence_note: Marks from the register's assessment of the same law (nsw-payroll-tax). Evidence on bunching is mixed: e61 found strong bunching at South Australia's threshold; Treasury found little at most states' thresholds before 2015.
